hints.S43_A1: It moves SLOWLY, and the BROAD, FLAT TAIL only steers - no effort, no splashing. Ask: which verb means to move smoothly and effortlessly? 'Raced' is fast, 'leaped' jumps, and 'dived' goes under.
hints.S43_A2: The fish is working AGAINST THE RIVER CURRENT and it uses its FINS. Ask: which verb means to keep something steady and balanced? 'Hide' conceals, 'push' presses, and 'dissolve' belongs to sugar in water.
hints.S43_A3: The water crosses ROCKS AND BOULDERS before it becomes CALM and FLAT. Ask: which verb describes rolling, churning movement over obstacles? 'Froze' and 'evaporated' would turn the water into something else.
hints.S43_A4: The dash gives the measurement: IT CAN GROW UP TO ONE AND A HALF METRES LONG. Ask: which adjective means impressively large and powerful? 'Tiny', 'invisible' and 'shy' all shrink the animal.
hints.S43_A5: The zone sits BETWEEN THE RIVER AND THE DRY LAND - neither one nor the other, but a gradual change from one into another. Ask: which word names a zone of change? 'Separate' would keep them apart.
hints.S43_B1: HAVE is already there, and MORE THAN THREE THOUSAND SPECIES have been counted up to now. Ask: after 'have', which form completes a present perfect - plain verb, -s form, -ing form, or past participle?
hints.S43_B2: The guides ANNOUNCED A SURPRISE RIVER CRUISE - a sudden event landing in the middle of something longer. Ask: which choice shows the family already busy at that past moment?
hints.S43_B3: 'World' tells you every river on Earth is compared - ONE winner among all of them, not two rivals. Ask: does a short adjective take -er or -est in that situation? And which little word stands in front of a superlative?
hints.S43_B4: SPECIES can be counted, and THAN ANY OTHER park sets two parks side by side. Ask: which quantity word raises one countable number above another? 'The most' would compare all parks at once; 'much' needs an uncountable noun.
hints.S43_B5: The statement is already NEGATIVE, and it happened in the past: she wondered about the FEEDING SCHEDULE then. Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag flip to positive or stay negative? The tag must keep the same tense.
hints.S43_B6: The frame is half-built already: NOT ___ PLENTIFUL ... SALTWATER. Ask: which single little word opens an equal-comparison frame, so that the negative in front turns it into 'less'? The two-part option would repeat a word already printed.
hints.S43_B7: The MANATEES do not care for themselves: TRAINED MARINE BIOLOGISTS do, and they MONITOR THEIR HEALTH DAILY, so it is still happening. Ask: which choice is passive, with the subject receiving the action, and set in the present?
hints.S43_B8: The conservationist is FORBIDDING an action near the RIVER OTTERS. Ask: after 'told + person', does a plain verb follow, an -ing form, or an infinitive with its little marker? And where does a negative word sit - ahead of that marker?
hints.S43_C1: The manatee is measured against ANY ANIMAL FOUND IN THE RIVER and comes out level - nothing is gentler, nothing rougher. Ask: which box structure marks an EQUAL comparison, with neither side higher?
hints.S43_C2: Otters spend MOST OF THE DAY HUNTING AND PLAYING, so their energy stands higher, not level. Ask: which box structure raises one side above another when the adjective is long, like ENERGETIC?
hints.S43_C3: OF ALL FRESHWATER ANIMALS compares one creature against every other, not against a single rival. Ask: which box phrase crowns a winner over a whole group? A two-way comparative would beat only one rival.
hints.S43_C4: DESPITE ITS FEARSOME REPUTATION tells you the true number of attacks is lower, not higher - and SWIMMERS can be counted one by one. Ask: which box structure lowers a COUNTABLE number? 'Less' needs something uncountable.
hints.S43_C5: LARGER is already a comparative, so it cannot take another comparing word in front of it. Ask: which box structure adds an intensifier meaning 'by a wide margin' to a word that already ends in -er?
hints.S43_C6: FRESHWATER CROCODILES are still to be respected, but SALTWATER CROCODILES are worse - and this clause carries no negative word yet. Ask: which box structure denies an equal comparison and so places one side lower?
hints.S43_C7: Two changes move together: go DEEPER, and it grows DARKER AND COLDER. Ask: which box structure pairs two comparatives so that one rises with another? Nothing here is measured against a second river.
hints.S43_C8: Nothing is being measured here - one option is chosen over another: NATURAL HABITAT wins over A LABORATORY TANK. Ask: which box phrase means 'instead of'? Comparative structures all need an adjective, and there is none.
hints.S43_D1: The dash defines it: A COMMUNITY OF LIVING THINGS THAT DEPEND ON EACH OTHER and on the water. Ask: which box word names a whole community plus its surroundings? 'Habitat' names only a home; 'current' is moving water.
hints.S43_D2: The clue sits just before the blank: THE SPEED OF THE WATER. Ask: which box word names that flow, slow in one place and fast in the RAPIDS? It follows 'or', so it must be a noun.
hints.S43_D3: The dash explains it: THOSE THAT LIVE IN WATER, with GILLS and WEBBED FEET. Ask: which box word is an adjective describing water-dwelling creatures? A noun cannot sit in front of 'animals' here.
hints.S43_D4: The blank follows 'Plants and certain organisms also', so it must be a verb, and the clue is REMOVING DIRT AND IMPURITIES. Ask: which box word means to clean water by passing it through something?
hints.S43_D5: Humans POLLUTE the river and destroy this, and MANY SPECIES DEPEND ON it to survive. Ask: which box word names the natural home of a plant or animal? 'Ecosystem' is the whole community, not the place one creature lives.
hints.S43_E1: Count them: THE OTTERS, SWIMMING IN TIGHT CIRCLES - more than one animal. Ask: does a plural subject take a singular past verb, or a plural one? Never match the verb to 'the class'.
hints.S43_E2: MOVED is an action verb, and the guide takes care SO THAT THE ANIMALS WOULD NOT BE STARTLED. Ask: do we describe an action with an adjective, or with an adverb ending in -ly?
hints.S43_E3: The weather was excessively HUMID - past the point of COMFORT. Ask: which spelling means 'excessively', and which one only shows direction? The meaning-word carries one extra letter.
hints.S43_E4: Read it again: ONE OTTER kept using its webbed feet, and this LONG, FLAT TAIL belongs to that single animal. Ask: how many owners are there, and where does the apostrophe go when there is only one?
hints.S43_E5: A SMALL GROUP grazing at the RIVERBANK - and this animal behaves like 'sheep' and 'fish'. Ask: does its plural take an -s at all, or does the word stay exactly the same?
hints.S43_F1: The two facts clash: freshwater is ONLY THREE PERCENT of all the water, yet nothing is more precious. Ask: which fact follows the contrast word, and which becomes the main clause? Replace the repeated subject with a pronoun.
hints.S43_F2: Which fact explains the other? HUNTS IN GROUPS is the cause; catching fish more easily is the result. Ask: does the reason follow the joining word, and where does the comma land? Use a pronoun for the second mention.
